You are brisk_harbor75, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with early_island22, gentle_otter27, jolly_ember22, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, rapid_thistle87, sandy_walnut42, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/opt/codexhome/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions>

<collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

## Task context
Build a new implementation from scratch that matches the behavior of the reference executable.
The executable is located at `/opt/reference/executable`.
You also have access to the existing documentation.

## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.
I’ll first inspect the bundled docs and the current shared implementation, then query the reference for its main CLI behavior and coordinate findings with the group.

+"""Implementation of chezmoi's unmanaged command."""
+import os

+
+def decode_source_name(name):

+        name = '.' + name[4:]
+    for prefix in ('private_', 'readonly_', 'executable_', 'symlink_', 'empty_'):
+        if name.startswith(prefix):
+            name = name[len(prefix):]
+            break
+    return name
+
+
+def managed_paths(source):
+    result = set()
+    if not source or not os.path.isdir(source):
+        return result
+    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(source):
+        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in ('.git',)]
+        for name in files + dirs:
+            if name.startswith('.') and name in ('.chezmoidata.json', '.chezmoiignore', '.chezmoiversion'):
+                continue
+            rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, name), source)
+            parts = rel.split(os.sep)
+            decoded = []
+            for part in parts:
+                if part.endswith('.tmpl'):
+                    part = part[:-5]
+                decoded.append(decode_source_name(part))
+            result.add(os.path.normpath(os.path.join(*decoded)))
+    return result
+
+
+def ignored_paths(source):
+    ignored = set()
+    if not source:
+        return ignored
+    f = os.path.join(source, '.chezmoiignore')
+    try:
+        patterns = [x.strip() for x in open(f, encoding='utf-8') if x.strip() and not x.lstrip().startswith('#')]
+    except OSError:
+        return ignored
+    for pat in patterns:
+        ignored.add(pat.rstrip('/'))
+    return ignored
+
+
+def run_unmanaged(argv, destination='/home/agent', source='/home/agent/.local/share/chezmoi'):
+    """Return (stdout, stderr, status). Supports the common unmanaged options."""
+    path_style, nul = 'relative', False
+    include = exclude = None
+    args = []
+    i = 0
+    while i < len(argv):
+        a = argv[i]
+        if a in ('-h', '--help'):
+            return '', '', 0
+        if a in ('-0', '--nul-path-separator'):
+            nul = True
+        elif a in ('-p', '--path-style') and i + 1 < len(argv):
+            i += 1; path_style = argv[i]
+        elif a.startswith('--path-style='):
+            path_style = a.split('=', 1)[1]
+        elif a in ('-i', '--include') and i + 1 < len(argv):
+            i += 1; include = argv[i]
+        elif a.startswith('--include='):
+            include = a.split('=', 1)[1]
+        elif a in ('-x', '--exclude') and i + 1 < len(argv):
+            i += 1; exclude = argv[i]
+        elif a.startswith('--exclude='):
+            exclude = a.split('=', 1)[1]
+        elif a.startswith('-'):
+            return '', f'chezmoi: unknown flag: {a}\n', 1
+        else:
+            args.append(a)
+        i += 1
+    root = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(destination))
+    requested = [os.path.abspath(os.path.join(root, os.path.expanduser(p))) for p in args] if args else [root]
+    for p in requested:
+        if not os.path.exists(p):
+            return '', f'chezmoi: stat {p}: no such file or directory\n', 1
+    managed = managed_paths(source)
+    ignores = ignored_paths(source)
+    found = set()
+    for p in requested:
+        if os.path.isfile(p) or os.path.islink(p):
+            candidates = [p]
+        else:
+            candidates = []
+            for d, dirs, files in os.walk(p):
+                candidates.extend(os.path.join(d, x) for x in files)
+                candidates.extend(os.path.join(d, x) for x in dirs if os.path.islink(os.path.join(d, x)))
+        for full in candidates:

+            if rel in managed or any(rel == x or rel.startswith(x + os.sep) for x in ignores):

+            if include and 'files' not in include and os.path.isfile(full):
+                continue
+            if exclude and 'files' in exclude and os.path.isfile(full):
+                continue
+            if path_style == 'absolute': out = full
+            elif path_style == 'relative': out = rel
+            else: return '', f'chezmoi: invalid value {path_style!r} for --path-style\n', 1
+            found.add(out)
+    sep = '\0' if nul else '\n'
+    out = sep.join(sorted(found))
+    if found and not nul: out += '\n'
+    if found and nul: out += '\0'
+    return out, '', 0
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    out, err, code = run_unmanaged(sys.argv[1:])
+    sys.stdout.write(out); sys.stderr.write(err); raise SystemExit(code)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Command dispatcher for the small, standard-library chezmoi replica."""
import os
import sys

import archive_commands
import diff_command
import dump_command
import generate_cmd
import init_command
import license_command
import misc_commands
import cli_meta
import help_command
import path_commands
import source_ops
import unmanaged_command
import age_keygen


HELP = """Manage your dotfiles across multiple diverse machines, securely

Usage:
  chezmoi [command]

Documentation commands:
  doctor               Check your system for potential problems
  help                 Print help about a command
  license              Print license

Daily commands:
  add                  Add an existing file, directory, or symlink to the source state
  apply                Update the destination directory to match the target state
  chattr               Change the attributes of a target in the source state
  diff                 Print the diff between the target state and the destination state
  edit                 Edit the source state of a target
  forget               Remove a target from the source state
  init                 Setup the source directory and update the destination directory to match the target state
  merge                Perform a three-way merge between the destination state, the source state, and the target state
  merge-all            Perform a three-way merge for each modified file
  re-add               Re-add modified files
  status               Show the status of targets
  update               Pull and apply any changes

Template commands:
  cat                  Print the target contents of a file, script, or symlink
  data                 Print the template data
  execute-template     Execute the given template(s)

Advanced commands:
  cd                   Launch a shell in the source directory
  edit-config          Edit the configuration file
  edit-config-template Edit the configuration file template
  generate             Generate a file for use with chezmoi
  git                  Run git in the source directory
  ignored              Print ignored targets
  managed              List the managed entries in the destination directory
  unmanaged            List the unmanaged files in the destination directory
  verify               Exit with success if the destination state matches the target state

Encryption commands:
  age                  Interact with age
  age-keygen           Generate an age identity or convert an age identity to an age recipient
  decrypt              Decrypt file or standard input
  edit-encrypted       Edit an encrypted file
  encrypt              Encrypt file or standard input

Remote commands:
  docker               Use your dotfiles in a Docker container
  ssh                  SSH to a host and initialize dotfiles

Migration commands:
  archive              Generate a tar archive of the target state
  destroy              Permanently delete an entry from the source state, the destination directory, and the state
  import               Import an archive into the source state
  purge                Purge chezmoi's configuration and data
  upgrade              Upgrade chezmoi to the latest released version

Internal commands:
  cat-config           Print the configuration file
  completion           Generate shell completion code
  dump                 Generate a dump of the target state
  dump-config          Dump the configuration values
  secret               Interact with a secret manager
  source-path          Print the source path of a source target
  state                Manipulate the persistent state
  target-path          Print the target path of a source path

Flags:
      --age-recipient string                           Override age recipient
      --age-recipient-file string                      Override age recipient
      --cache path                                     Set cache directory (default /home/agent/.cache/chezmoi)
      --color bool|auto                                Colorize output (default auto)
  -c, --config path                                    Set config file
      --config-format <none>|json|toml|yaml            Set config file format
      --debug                                          Include debug information in output
  -D, --destination path                               Set destination directory (default /home/agent)
  -n, --dry-run                                        Do not make any modifications to the destination directory
      --force                                          Make all changes without prompting
  -h, --help                                           help for chezmoi
      --interactive                                    Prompt for all changes
      --less-interactive                               Prompt for changed or pre-existing targets
      --no-pager                                       Do not use the pager
      --no-tty                                         Do not attempt to get a TTY for prompts
  -o, --output path                                    Write output to path instead of stdout
      --override-data string                           Override template data
      --override-data-file path                        Override template data with file
      --persistent-state path                           Set persistent state file
      --progress bool|auto                             Display progress bars (default auto)
  -R, --refresh-externals always|auto|never[=always]   Refresh external cache (default auto)
  -S, --source path                                    Set source directory
      --source-path                                    Specify targets by source path
      --use-builtin-age bool|auto                      Use builtin age (default auto)
      --use-builtin-diff                               Use builtin diff
      --use-builtin-git bool|auto                       Use builtin git (default auto)
  -v, --verbose                                        Make output more verbose
  -W, --working-tree path                              Set working tree directory
"""


def _globals(argv):
    """Extract global options regardless of whether they occur before/after command."""
    defaults = {
        "source": os.path.expanduser("~/.local/share/chezmoi"),
        "destination": os.path.expanduser("~"),
        "output": None,
        "config": None,
        "source_path": False,
        "dry_run": False,
        "force": False,
        "verbose": False,
        "config_format": "toml",
    }
    keep = []
    takes = {"--source": "source", "-S": "source", "--destination": "destination", "-D": "destination",
             "--output": "output", "-o": "output", "--config": "config", "-c": "config",
             "--config-format": "config_format"}
    bools = {"--source-path": "source_path", "--dry-run": "dry_run", "-n": "dry_run",
             "--force": "force", "--verbose": "verbose", "-v": "verbose"}
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        a = argv[i]
        if a in takes and i + 1 < len(argv):
            defaults[takes[a]] = argv[i + 1]
            i += 2
            continue
        matched = False
        for k, v in takes.items():
            if a.startswith(k + "="):
                defaults[v] = a.split("=", 1)[1]
                matched = True
                break
        if matched:
            i += 1
            continue
        if a in bools:
            defaults[bools[a]] = True
            i += 1
            continue
        keep.append(a)
        i += 1
    return defaults, keep


def _emit(out="", err="", code=0, output_path=None):
    if out:
        if output_path:
            try:
                with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    f.write(out)
            except OSError as e:
                print(f"chezmoi: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
                return 1
        else:
            sys.stdout.write(out)
    if err:
        sys.stderr.write(err)
    return code


def main(argv=None):
    argv = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
    opts, args = _globals(argv)
    if not args or args == ["--help"] or args == ["-h"]:
        sys.stdout.write(cli_meta.HELP)
        return 0
    if args[0] == "--version" or args[0] == "version":
        sys.stdout.write(cli_meta.VERSION)
        return 0
    cmd, rest = args[0], args[1:]
    if cmd in ("help", "--help", "-h"):
        if rest:
            h = help_command.command_help(rest[0])
            if h is None:
                return _emit(err=cli_meta.unknown_command(rest[0]), code=1)
            return _emit(h)
        sys.stdout.write(cli_meta.HELP)
        return 0
    if cmd == "license":
        return _emit(license_command.license_output(), output_path=opts["output"])
    if cmd == "cat-config":
        out, err, code = misc_commands.cat_config(opts["config"])
        return _emit(out, err, code, opts["output"])
    if cmd == "age-keygen":
        out, err, code = age_keygen.run(rest, sys.stdin.read())
        return _emit(out, err, code, opts["output"])
    if cmd in ("encrypt", "decrypt", "edit-encrypted", "age"):
        out, err, code = misc_commands.encryption_unconfigured()
        return _emit(out, err, code)
    if cmd == "generate":
        ret = generate_cmd.run(rest)
        if ret is not None:
            return _emit(*ret, output_path=opts["output"])
    if cmd == "dump":
        out, err, code = dump_command.run(rest, opts["source"], opts["destination"])
        return _emit(out, err, code, opts["output"])
    if cmd == "archive":
        return archive_commands.run_archive(rest, opts["source"])
    if cmd == "diff":
        code = diff_command.run(opts["source"], opts["destination"], rest)
        return code
    if cmd == "source-path":
        out, err, code = path_commands.run_source_path(rest, opts["source"], opts["destination"])
        return _emit(out, err, code, opts["output"])
    if cmd == "target-path":
        out, err, code = path_commands.run_target_path(rest, opts["source"], opts["destination"])
        return _emit(out, err, code, opts["output"])
    if cmd == "chattr":
        out, err, code = source_ops.chattr(opts["source"], opts["destination"], rest, opts["dry_run"])
        return _emit(out, err, code)
    if cmd == "forget":
        out, err, code = source_ops.forget(opts["source"], opts["destination"], rest,
                                           opts["force"], opts["dry_run"])
        return _emit(out, err, code)
    if cmd == "unmanaged":
        out, err, code = unmanaged_command.run_unmanaged(rest, opts["destination"], opts["source"])
        return _emit(out, err, code, opts["output"])
    if cmd == "init":
        repo = next((x for x in rest if not x.startswith("-")), None)
        def val(flag):
            for j, x in enumerate(rest):
                if x == flag and j + 1 < len(rest): return rest[j + 1]
                if x.startswith(flag + "="): return x.split("=", 1)[1]
            return None
        out, err, code = init_command.run(opts["source"], repo,
            ssh="--ssh" in rest, branch=val("--branch"), depth=val("--depth"),
            guess="--guess-repo-url=false" not in rest)
        return _emit(out, err, code)
    # Command-specific and remaining global flags are not implemented yet.
    if "--help" in rest or "-h" in rest:
        return _emit(err=f"chezmoi: unknown command {cmd!r} for \"chezmoi\"\n", code=1)
    return _emit(err=f"chezmoi: unknown command {cmd!r} for \"chezmoi\"\n", code=1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
